Ben / Chloe,

Thanks — quick context from our side so you can tailor the options:
- Budget target for 2027 pilot: ~$60k for first quarter (we can stretch slightly for a short trial if value is proven)
- Likely traffic: bursty inference during weekdays, sporadic nights/weekend; peaky prompts for batch exports at month-end
- Key asks: clear downgrade mechanics (if we drop from "scale" to "standard" mid-contract), and an explanation of how feature bundling (e.g., vector search + reranking add-on) is priced against throughput.

Procurement is looped in for contract language. At a minimum they need:
1) A sample amendment showing prorated credits for unused reserved capacity;
2) SLA fallback wording if redwood auto-failover routes to a lower-cost model during capacity constraints;
3) An estimated implementation timeline and calendar.

Happy to host a short workshop early next week to walk through two assemblies: a conservative Standard pack, and a Throughput+ pack we could pilot.

Thanks for the context, Ellen — this is helpful. I attached a focused pack comparison (packaging-options-v2.pdf) and two supporting sheets: CureStack-MAP.xlsx (traffic map + bill impact) and redwood-pricing-matrix.csv (unit math).

Summary of recommended assemblies (short):
- Standard (recommended for conservative pilots): shared-hosting, token-metered base, includes basic vector search; good for low-latency interactive flows.
- Throughput+ (recommended if month-end batch/export heavy): reserved capacity pool (dedicated GPUs), includes batching optimizations and KV caching; add-on for reranking + embeddings at a bundled discount.
- Progressive Pilot (3-month bridge): Start on Standard with a 30% step-up credit applied to first month of Throughput+ if you convert within 90 days. This reduces pilot friction.

Downgrade / fallback credit mechanics:
- If CureStack downgrades from Throughput+ to Standard mid-term, we offer a prorated credit for the unused reserved capacity calculated as: (unused committed hours * reserved rate) minus a 10% administrative conversion adjustment. Credits apply to future invoices within 90 days.
- If the platform routes traffic to a lower-cost model due to regional capacity constraints, the SLA fallback triggers a compensation credit equal to the token-rate difference for the affected window (documented in the SLA addendum).

Feature bundling note: bundling is priced as a % uplift to base throughput in our model matrix. For example, embeddings + rerank bundled together are ~18% cheaper overall than adding both as standalone metered add-ons (see redwood-pricing-matrix.csv line items). We can convert that uplift into a fixed monthly addon for straightforward procurement.

Ask from CureStack before we finalize:
- Confirm expected average concurrent requests during peak (Ellen, your ops team’s ballpark); the MAP sheet has columns you can fill which will give us a deterministic price.
- Confirm whether procurement prefers credits on invoice or a contractual credit ledger (we can do either).

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min workshop Mon/Tue to walk attachments and pick one assembly.
2) If you choose Throughput+, Ben will propose amendment language; Lauren will confirm discount eligibility.

Attachments referenced: packaging-options-v2.pdf, CureStack-MAP.xlsx, redwood-pricing-matrix.csv (links to each attached file).

Best,

We can support the Progressive Pilot route Chloe outlined. Commercial offers:

- Downgrade mechanics: we prefer invoice-applied credits (easier for finance) but can also bake credits into contract language if procurement prefers a ledger.
- Administrative note: the conversion adjustment Chloe mentioned (10%) is negotiable; for CureStack I can reduce it to 5% if we get a two-week commit to a go-live window.

I'll draft a short contract amendment and a one-page commercial summary for procurement (DocuSign-ready). Ben — want me to include the 15% concession in the sheet Chloe attached or keep it separate?
